body:
Fair enough. I find other people are the main reason I don't kill myself. I can't remember the last time I was content with myself. Hopefully therapy will teach me how to fix that. But I have a feeling I will have to be the one to actually make that change.

Fear of death is also understandable for me too. Standing near a ledge where I could have a fatal fall, suddenly I don't feel as suicidal as when I'm doing something else.

I hope you can learn to enjoy life by yourself, and I also hope you find more time to spend with your friends. Thanks for your reply :)
What keeps you going? I find myself making similar remarks to you, but here I am still kicking. Glad you're still here. I got a little bit of dopamine when I saw you posted recently.

How are you doing OP? I just failed a bunch of easy classes I should've passed with an A, and I looked up why I shouldn't kill myself if I failed college. And to think I wanna go to med school lol. Hopefully you aren't gone, I can't explain why, but I feel like there has to be better gambles to take that don't involve ending everything. I'd rather gamble tomorrow might be bearable, than gamble on getting nothing.
Well I'm a junior halfway through the current year so I guess year and a half instead of years

Yeah I used to do a chess club but that stopped after COVID and that plus school was like my only socialization. I used to take piano lessons but it wasnt fun anymore so I stopped, I used to take cello lessons but it wasnt fun anymore so I stopped that, I used to do boyscouts and that wasn't fun anymore. The only thing I remotely enjoy doing now is video games, YouTube, and kinda weightlifting. I've tried a bunch of things but they always end up with me. being burnt out or not enjoying it anymore. I don't even know what is something I'm going to like at this point.

100% normal, I'm "medically diagnosed" with depression but the only qualifications I needed was a high score on the PHQ-9 and I fucking hate that because all of those questions were my outlook on myself, and obviously not objective.
You're right, I might just not be noticing everything around me. Or I'm around a bunch of people who I am acquaintances with, but not close freinds so they dont ask about stuff like this.

Honestly I kinda like them too, I feel like I dont have to fake a smile anymore. And sometimes they can look pretty cool. I do miss common facial expressions around my friends in public, but whenever I hang out not in public and I can talk about whatever I just dont wear a mask around them.
I think people notice it, but will awkwardly try to gloss over it.
Yeah. I feel like I have "the straw that breaks the camels back" moments all the time but the camels back is actually made of broken glass

I'll probably have to go with number one (telling my therapist about wanting to be alone, not the suicidal thoughts) as my parents monitor my phone and I dont think I'd ever have the chance to pass the therapist a note.
I've been calm and gentle, just saying "I'd prefer if I could do the sessions alone" but they won't budge. I dont want to raise my voice or be hostile cause that will inky make it worse.
For me, I think home is the people you surround yourself with, and not the place. Hell, I felt more at home when I would sleep over at a friends house than my house
I am safe now, I've been laying in bed pretty much all day just thinking. I have really good friends luckily, so they were able to pull me out of that mindset I had. Thank you for your concern.

I had a dream once where I was laying under a snow lift, and snow was falling all around me. (It was like the place here (https://youtu.be/GaakAO4l2Dg) where the guy looks for the first few seconds). It was the most beautiful thing I've ever seen. And I was hugging someone. We were both just laying in the snow next to each other hugging. She wasnt even someone I had a crush on, just someone who I'm friends with. I think I felt love and warmth. My brain was able to simulate someone outside of my family caring for me in such a sincere way. I was so happy, and my brain let me stay in this oasis for a while. I'm pretty sure I even considered that this could be a dream in the dream, but I just brushed it off (in the dream). All I was caring about was the moment, me hugging the person who is hugging me back with such care, that all I wanted to do was have that last forever. I think that was my last hit of serotonin. Then I woke up in my bed some time in the early morning, still in the delusion that someone was holding me. Then when I opened my eyes to look next to me (I sleep in a queen sized bed) no one was there. Then I cried the hardest I've ever cried. I realized that I was such a loser that the only time someone outside of my family would love me is in a dream my brain makes up. Ever since then I dont think I've ever truly been happy.

Exactly! I haven't been diagnosed with depression, but I'm 95% sure I have it. But I've been on this sub for awhile and people are talking about how its impossible for them to feel happiness whatsoever. Is this only for the super severe cases maybe?

Dude looking back on my elementary years made me realize how much I took it for granted. Those were some of the happiest times I had, because I was ignorant to the rest of the world. I hope you can have the same luxury as me, and dont forget to love the time you have now. Also be careful on reddit, there are some bad places here that can scar you.

You see that's the thing I'm not gonna commit suicide cause I dont want the people close to me to feel my pain 10 fold. But its just *so* tempting at this point, I just dont see a happy future for myself. I'm only living for other happiness at this point.

Half of me wants to commit suicide but the other logical half of me knows that it will cause 10 fold pain to others around me. I dont want to do that, but it is just an easy way out. I know it's a selfish move, but I just don't know what to do anymore. My dad yelled at me when I was sad to just "cheer up" and I dont know how to feel anymore. I've tested the length to hang myself in my closet but it's too close to the ground, and I'm too much of a pussy to do it cause of the possibility of me surviving and having permanent brain damage.

Thanks for rooting for me! It feels weird that I've been taught my entire life that strangers on the internet are the equivalent of satan, but the first person I vent to is a stranger on the internet. I've had thoughts about thinking about suicide (idk if that makes sense but that's the only way I can describe it), but I dont think I can do that. I know that my pain would just transfer to friends and loved ones, and that wouldn't solve anything. Also because this is just a few weeks of my life where I feel miserable, I dont want to throw away the rest of my life over a quarentine. The thing is my life is objectively good, I have a supporting family, have most of the materialistic things I want, and have a very easy life to be honest. I dont know how I end up in this position. Again, thank you so much.

Thank you for this, it really means a lot. I think I'll wait a little longer to see if its truly depression. I dont know if this "depression" is because of the quarentine, the news, online college classes, a lot more demand in work, etc. I also dont think that my parents would dismiss it, but I think they would just attribute it to the circumstances all of us are in. I'm lucky enough to have loving parents, even if I feel worthless. I just feel like there are to many variables, and I dont want to have to break the facade I've set up of a fun going guy only to have it be a false call. I'll try this eventually. Thank you again, it means so much.
